chapter_note: This chapter is largely cosmological teaching about the Third Ambassador’s displayed Image and the rulers’ imitation that results in Adam and Eve, plus a short doctrinal appendix on other non-sexually-generated figures (sea-giant, sea-monster, vegetation). The main later material is (a) the dialogue/Q&A frame (¶1–2) and (b) the extended worldly parable of the ‘free woman’ (¶5–6) and brief exhortative closure (¶8). No NT citation vectors appear; the key discriminator is cosmos→cosmos exposition versus cosmos→worldly illustration.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Hagiographic Q&A container: ‘disciples questioned… they say to him…’ The paragraph is presented as disciples’ argument, not impersonal system exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.133⟩ Regarding the Ambassador, the occasion when he came displaying his image, he [d]id not come so th[a]t he might reveal his image to the ru[l]ers in the universe. Rather, he came and displayed to the universe be[cause of h]is soul and his son, who is [ ... ] every [ ... ], that he might enable him to live [ ... ] and make for him a release; and to free (the soul) from every bond and all the fetters, in which it is entangled and bound.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue attribution/frame: “Then speaks the glorious one to his disciples:”
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core cosmological mechanism (purpose of the Image-display: release/freeing of the soul) embedded inside a formal speech-attribution frame.

paragraphs.core_text: Still, you, look and see! The rulers and the authorities, in that they had no form in [ ... ] him, they lusted for his image. They reflected upon themselves, that [they] had no [one] like him in their creation. They sealed hi[s im]a[g]e in their heart, within their soul. Afterward[s, they] built it according to his likeness; they formed Adam and [Ev]e. They sealed the image of the exalted one in their [soul]. So, they [co]pied with an imitation; but they have not [copied i]n truth! Rather, just as [ ... ... ] it is made as these, for [i]t came [ ... ] but it is not l[ik]e him in truth. [Again, so too] is this figure of ma[nkind. They copi]ed it against the image of the exalted one [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological explanation of how the rulers originate Adam/Eve via imitation of the displayed Image; stays within cosmic agents/processes (rulers/authorities/Image/sealing). Minor second-person rhetoric does not introduce institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: Similarly the [t]ree, for while it is like the [ ... it is] not [copi]ed in truth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Brief correspondential analogy supporting the ‘imitation not truth’ argument; no frame or institutional pointing.

Extended worldly parable (free woman, chamber, city, nobles/servants) used as illustrative application; mapping crosses from cosmic system into social-world staging, characteristic of later explanatory expansion.

Continuation of the same worldly simile, explicitly applying it (‘In accord with this simile…’). Though it names the Ambassador, the paragraph’s vehicle remains a worldly illustrative story rather than system description.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, this too is the way of the Third Ambassador, when he came and display[ed his] image with a show towards all the powers. [He did] not [co]me so that all the rulers and the author[it]ies would sculpt a form [after h]is likeness. R[ather], he came because of his son being crucified in the totality; [fo]r he would release him, free him, and rescue him from oppres-sion. Yet, when the rulers looked o[n] him, [th]ey lusted for his image. They fashioned after his [like]ness Adam and Eve, without the consent of the gre[at]ness.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic cosmological rationale (Image-display for rescue/release; rulers’ lust → fashioning Adam/Eve). ‘Crucified in the totality’ functions as Manichaean cosmic process language here, not a Gospel citation.
Direct address/exhortative closure (‘I have enlightened you… commit it to memory’), marking editorial/pedagogical application voice rather than cosmological mechanism.

paragraphs.core_text: [Understa]nd also this other (matter) that I will teach you. For, [a]s with Adam and Eve, whom the rulers fashioned and [se]aled after the image of the exalted one, so too this [i]s how a manifold divinity and many powers and angels [ ... received] the stamp of that image, which was displayed to them. For, in the majesty of the l[ig]ht and (the image's) love, they glowed with their desire and they were undone. Th[ey] were eager for their lust;
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed introductory teacher-address clause and the ensuing worldly simile beginning “like a m[an who looks] to the majesty of a lusted after face…” because it shifts from cosmological description to human-world illustration.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core claim: many powers/angels receive the stamp of the displayed Image; later explanatory flourish adds a human lust simile (cosmos→world), indicating secondary illustrative expansion.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.136⟩ This is [als]o the case with those powers, when they looked on that majestic and beautiful [imag]e, they () [ ... ] a first image. They received the stamp of th[at image], which was displayed to them. They copied [ ... wh]ich th[ey co]pied out in a likeness, it being made [ ... ... ] the ones that they had put forth, which had received a [stamp of this im]age; but inward even to the rocks [ ... ... ] which occur from place to place. The {} of that image, which was displayed in the universe [ ... ] they received a stamp, it being revealed there, and an impress.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal continuation of the ‘stamp/impress’ mechanism applied across powers and even rocks; remains internal to the cosmological/correspondential system (image → imprint → forms).

paragraphs.core_text: Now, this new birth that they begot in a new [ ... ] in the world, is Adam and Eve. [There is not a] form in their world since the beginning like it; because that [im]age [occ]urs not in the worlds b[el]ow.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmological negative-argument: the Image-form does not occur in the lower worlds; therefore the ‘new birth’ is anomalous. Despite the ‘Now’ connective, it stays in system-description.

paragraphs.core_text: Not all the figures that have been fashioned were fashioned by birth from displayed intercourse. Rather, there are other figures fashioned [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: General doctrinal proposition about modes of generation of forms (not solely sexual intercourse), setting up a numbered exempla list—typical teaching-core structure.

paragraphs.core_text: One of them is the sea [gi]ant, the 'sweeping' from the sphere, which the [Father] of Life discharged into the sea. Its own fire and thought fashioned it [in] a figure.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mythic-cosmological exemplum with named divine agent (Father of Life) and internal formative faculties (‘fire and thought’)—system exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: The second figure is the one [that] fell to the earth. It made the sea its womb. Its own l[us]t became its sculptor. It alone fashioned it to a nature, which is the root of death. Yet, when it came up from the sea, it [ ... ] that it might destroy the works [ ... ] of Life. They immediately sent against it the Adamant of Light, the great 'instruction of vigour'. He humbled it in the districts of the north. He has trampled underfoot and set h[im]self upon it, until the end of the world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic combat/process narrative (lust as sculptor; Adamant of Light sent; north districts; until end of world) remains within the Manichaean cosmic architecture, not institutional application.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.137⟩ [The] third figure is the nature that fell on wh[at] is dr[y. It] fashioned the tree and set itself there. [ ... the] new figure that was fashioned [ ... d]isplays.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third exemplum completing the triad (sea giant / sea monster / vegetation-tree). Numbered exempla lists are a common core-teaching vehicle.

paragraphs.core_text: So, in accord with the essence they [ ... the dark]ness; but yet th[ey] did not come with the King of Dark[ness to the wo]rld. Rather, their fashioning [came] about [ ... ] they are composite and have been displayed in the world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Concluding cosmological classification: these figures are ‘composite’ and not simply imported with the King of Darkness—system-level ontological sorting, characteristic of the oldest explanatory layer.
